root_cause.text: The discovery table parsing logic failed to validate that a die ID is within the valid range of online dies, allowing array indexing beyond the allocated bounds of the `pmu->boxes` array when processing devices from offline dies.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `(die >= uncore_max_dies())` to the existing validation at line 374 in `uncore_discovery_pci()`. Previously, only `die < 0` was checked, but when all CPUs in a die are offline (particularly in NUMA-disabled systems with fewer CPUs than die 0 capacity), the die ID could be valid but exceed the number of online dies tracked by `uncore_max_dies()`. This caused `pmu->boxes[die]` to overflow in `uncore_pci_pmu_register()` at line 1157, triggering the warning. The fix ensures discovery table entries for offline dies are skipped by validating the die ID against the actual online die count.

intent_record.what: Modified the conditional check from `if (die < 0)` to `if ((die < 0) || (die >= uncore_max_dies()))` to add an upper bound validation on the die variable.
intent_record.how: The change adds a boundary check to ensure the die ID is not only non-negative but also does not exceed the maximum number of dies supported by the system. This prevents out-of-bounds access or invalid die indices from being processed in the subsequent parse_discovery_table() call.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the `uncore_insert_box_info()` function at line 147: `type->box_ctrl_die[die] = unit->ctl;`. This array indexing uses the `die` parameter without validating that it is within the valid range of online dies. The `die` value comes from `get_device_die_id(dev)` (line 289) which can return any value including -1 for offline CPUs (line 56), but the code at line 289 only checks `if (die < 0) continue;` to skip processing.
